newsitem.title: NORWAY: SAS sees H1 pre-tax around SKR 1 bln - report.
newsitem.headline: SAS sees H1 pre-tax around SKR 1 bln - report.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) expects first-half profits before tax of around one billion Swedish crowns ($126.4 million) following a sharp increase in passenger traffic in the second quarter, the financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv (DN) said on Friday.
In the first quarter SAS posted a pre-tax loss of 269 million crowns.

"The figures for April, May and June are so positive that everything indicates that we will achieve the same result in the first half this year as the same period last year," Peter Forssman, SAS chief spokesman, told the daily.
SAS, which is jointly owned by the governments of Denmark, Sweden and Norway and private investors, reported a pre-tax result in the first half 1996 of 1.05 billion crowns.
Danish analysts told DN it would be surprising if SAS had made up losses from the first quarter to bring the half-year result in line with 1996.
"That means that SAS must have profits of around 1.3 billion crowns in the second quarter in order to achieve that," DN quoted one analyst as saying.
Danish analysts' expectations for SAS pre-tax profits in the second quarter are between 700 million crowns and one billion crowns, the daily said.

It said that SAS shares on the Oslo bourse have climbed 71 percent since the end of March in reaction to a rise in monthly passenger figures. In June SAS reported a 6.5 percent increase in passenger traffic from the corresponding period a year ago.
The share was also boosted by an analysis by Britain's NatWest Securities which said SAS was undervalued and that the share price would rise 40 percent in the next year.
On Thursday SAS shares in Oslo closed at 112 Norwegian crowns.
